drafts.title: Exterior charge-port indicator clearly shows charging state at a glance
drafts.description: Customers can tell from outside the car whether charging is not active, charging, fully charged, or there is a charging error by looking at the charge-port area without using the app or opening the door.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: The exterior charge-port indicator uses distinct, easily distinguishable visual signals for Off / Charging / Full / Error that are legible from 3 meters in daylight and at night; in a usability test with 30 participants, 95% correctly identify the state within 3 seconds.
assumptions: Exterior indicator can use multiple colors/patterns legally permitted and visible under direct sunlight.
Vehicle production tolerances and placement will allow visibility from typical curb-side viewing angles.
uncertainties: Regulatory restrictions on exterior lighting color/patterns in some markets may require minor signal adjustments.

drafts.title: Navigation suggests compatible fast chargers and shows connector and availability en route
drafts.description: When planning a long trip, customers get route suggestions that list only fast chargers compatible with the vehicle, show connector/adapter requirements and estimated available stalls, and minimize detours for charging.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: On a set of 50 representative multi-stop long-distance routes (aggregate 25,000 miles of routes) the navigation suggests chargers compatible with the vehicle for at least 95% of required charging stops and displays connector type and real-time reported stall availability for at least 85% of those suggested chargers.
assumptions: Access to live charger metadata and availability from major roaming/charging networks is contracted.
Compatibility mapping (plug types, charging profiles) between vehicle and charger networks is maintained and updated regularly.
uncertainties: Coverage and data quality of third-party charging networks vary by region and may affect availability indicator accuracy.

drafts.title: Offer a powertrain option that delivers at least 600 miles real-world range on one tank or full charge
drafts.description: Customers who want the longest single-trip distance can choose a 5 Series variant that achieves at least 600 miles in typical real-world driving without needing a refill or recharge.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: A defined real-world mixed cycle (70% highway at 70 mph / 30% urban), conducted as the median of five independent runs under ambient conditions 10–30°C with two occupants and no roof load, must show a range ≥ 600 miles for the variant advertised as '600-mile range'.
assumptions: This outcome may be achieved via an efficient combustion/hybrid powertrain or a high-capacity BEV variant; market demand and regulatory environment allow offering such a powertrain in the successor range.
Fuel energy density improvements or battery energy-density improvements continue at modest pace enabling competitive range by successor launch.
uncertainties: Achieving 600 miles for a BEV depends strongly on battery energy density and vehicle mass; if those do not progress as assumed, the 600-mile option may require a combustion or Hybrid solution.
Real-world range is highly dependent on driving style, load and climate; customers may not achieve advertised range in all conditions.

drafts.title: Improve ride comfort on broken pavement so trips feel less harsh
drafts.description: Customers experience noticeably reduced harshness over broken or patched pavement compared with the current 5 Series, with fewer jarring vertical impacts transmitted to occupants.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: On a standardized rough-road track (defined test section with repeated potholes and patched surfaces) at 30–50 mph, objective vertical-acceleration RMS at seat mounts must be reduced by at least 15% versus the current model baseline and a validated occupant comfort survey must show a 20% improvement in perceived harshness (N=25).
assumptions: Successor chassis and suspension designs allow tuning to reduce vertical acceleration without compromising safety or handling expectations.
Road test facility with repeatable rough-surface profile is available for validation.
uncertainties: Trade-offs between ride comfort and dynamic handling may require variant-specific tuning; improvements for average customers may not meet all driving-style preferences.

drafts.title: Reduce distracting wind noise at highway speeds above 70 mph
drafts.description: Customers experience lower wind-driven cabin noise at sustained highway speeds so long-distance driving is less fatiguing and conversations are easier.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: At 75 mph on a certified highway noise track with windows closed and HVAC off, the interior A-weighted sound pressure level from exterior wind sources at the driver's ear position must be ≤ 67 dB(A) and subjective annoyance scores (N=20) must improve by at least 25% vs the current model.
assumptions: Measurement uses standardized microphone placement and a consistent test environment (wind, road, tires controlled).
Exterior sealing, mirror and body-flow improvements are feasible within successor packaging constraints.
uncertainties: Actual on-road results vary with tire choice, roof load and side-window sealing wear over vehicle life.

drafts.title: Lane-keeping assistance steers smoothly through curves without abrupt corrections
drafts.description: When Lane Keeping Assist (LKA) is active, customers feel smooth, predictable steering inputs in curves rather than abrupt snap-back or nervous corrections.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: In a set of curved road tests at speeds 50–70 mph and curve radii 150–500 m, automated steering lateral-acceleration slew rates (change in lateral acceleration) must be limited so that peak rate < 0.2 m/s² per second and in a user study (N=30) perceived steering abruptness is reduced by at least 40% versus the current model.
assumptions: Vehicle control systems can be tuned to prioritize smoothness over aggressive lane-centering when the driver has hands detected on the wheel and no imminent collision risk.
Test routes include a representative mix of highway curves and on-/off-ramps.
uncertainties: Edge-case scenarios (sudden evasive maneuvers) may still require abrupt steering interventions for safety; tuning must balance comfort and safety.
Different drivers have different preferences for LKA behavior; personalization options may be necessary.

drafts.title: Request for Level 3 automated-driving type approval in Germany (regulatory request — out of scope)
drafts.description: Customers ask that the vehicle receives type approval for Level 3 automated driving in Germany.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: This item is a regulatory/homologation request rather than a customer-facing product outcome; decisions and compliance activities for type approval belong to regulatory and legal processes and will be tracked separately by the homologation team.
drafts.scope_reason: Regulatory / homologation request — outside product requirement specification. Implementation depends on type-approval decisions, legal/regulatory frameworks and certification activities.

drafts.title: Request that powertrain complies with CARB (California) emission limits (regulatory request — out of scope)
drafts.description: Customers ask that the powertrain complies with CARB emission limits in all US states.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: This is a regulatory compliance requirement; tracking and fulfillment require homologation and emissions certification work by engineering and regulatory teams rather than a customer-facing product feature.
drafts.scope_reason: Regulatory / emissions compliance request — outside product feature scope and handled via certification/homologation processes.

drafts.title: UN R155 cybersecurity type-approval request (regulatory request — out of scope)
drafts.description: Customers ask that the vehicle fulfils UN R155 cybersecurity type approval.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: UN R155 conformance is a regulatory/certification activity; cybersecurity design and certification plans will be handled by the responsible engineering and compliance teams rather than as a consumer-facing requirement draft here.
drafts.scope_reason: Regulatory / certification request — outside the scope of customer-facing product requirements.

drafts.title: Battery passport regulation compliance (regulatory request — out of scope)
drafts.description: Customers ask that the vehicle battery complies with the EU battery passport regulation.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Compliance with EU battery passport rules is a regulatory requirement and will be addressed by compliance/engineering delivery plans; it is not expressed here as a customer-facing specification.
drafts.scope_reason: Regulatory compliance request — belongs to certification/compliance workstreams.

drafts.title: Request for 800 V electrical architecture (engineering spec — out of scope)
drafts.description: Customers ask that the car uses an 800 V electrical architecture.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: This is an explicit engineering-architecture request. Decisions on voltage architecture and associated trade-offs (packaging, cost, suppliers) are engineering decisions and thus recorded here as out of scope for customer-facing requirements.
drafts.scope_reason: Engineering architecture request — a supplier/architecture-level decision that is outside direct customer-facing requirement scope.

drafts.title: Request to upgrade onboard AC charger to 22 kW (engineering spec — out of scope)
drafts.description: Customers ask that the onboard AC charger is upgraded to 22 kW.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: This is a specific electrical engineering specification request; decisions to change onboard charger rating will be assessed by engineering for feasibility and product variants and are out of scope for customer-facing requirements here.
drafts.scope_reason: Engineering specification (onboard charger kW) — outside the remit of customer-facing functional requirements.

drafts.title: Request for solid-state battery cells rated at ~400 Wh/kg (engineering spec — out of scope)
drafts.description: Customers ask that the battery uses solid-state cells achieving roughly 400 Wh/kg.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: This is a material/chemistry-level request. Deployment of specific cell chemistry and energy-density targets is an engineering and supply-chain decision and is recorded here as out of scope for customer-facing requirements.
drafts.scope_reason: Engineering / cell-chemistry request — belongs to battery engineering and supplier roadmap decisions.

drafts.title: Request for front brake-disc diameter of 395 mm (engineering spec — out of scope)
drafts.description: Customers ask that the front brake discs have a diameter of 395 mm.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: This is a detailed hardware-dimension request; braking hardware sizing is an engineering decision that depends on vehicle variant and packaging and is therefore out of scope for customer-facing requirements.
drafts.scope_reason: Hardware-dimension request — an engineering specification best handled in component/variant design processes.

drafts.title: Request to source lidar from a named supplier for highway assist (supplier-spec request — out of scope)
drafts.description: Customers ask that highway assist uses a lidar sensor from a named supplier.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: This is a supplier-selection request. Choice of specific sensor suppliers is a procurement/engineering decision and is out of scope for customer-facing requirements; highway assist performance requirements should be expressed in functional terms instead.
drafts.scope_reason: Supplier selection request — procurement/engineering decision outside the customer-facing requirement set.
